lessons.title: Non-Fiction: What Makes Something Alive?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about living things from a non-fiction text.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about living things.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a non-fiction text about what makes something alive.
lessons.independent_task: Children read an extract and answer retrieval questions.
key_questions: Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap facts found about living things.
lessons.home_link: Find a fact about living things at home.

lessons.title: Introducing Thirds
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to find a third of a shape or quantity.
success_criteria: I can find a third of a shape.
I can find a third of a quantity.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap halves and quarters from Year 1.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model finding a third of shapes (dividing into 3 equal parts) and quantities.
lessons.independent_task: Children find a third of given shapes and quantities, recording answers.
key_questions: What is a third of this shape?
What is a third of 9 counters?

differentiation.support: Find a third of quantities to 9 with counters
differentiation.greater_depth: Find a third of quantities to 30

lessons.assessment_notes: Record introduction of thirds, a new Year 2 fraction — evidence for MATHS.N4.
lessons.home_link: Find a third of a group of objects at home.

lessons.title: Signs of Life
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify signs that indicate something is alive.
success_criteria: I can name a sign of life.
I can use it to decide if something is alive.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss signs of life (move, grow, need food/water, reproduce, breathe, sense).
lessons.independent_task: Children use signs of life to decide and justify whether objects/organisms are alive.
key_questions: Does it move on its own?

differentiation.support: Use 2-3 signs of life with support
differentiation.greater_depth: Use all signs of life to justify tricky examples

lessons.assessment_notes: Note deeper reasoning about classification criteria — evidence for SCI.LIV.
lessons.home_link: Decide if 3 things at home are alive, dead, or never alive.

lessons.title: Writing About Living Things
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write factual sentences explaining why something is alive.
success_criteria: I can write why something is alive.
I can use a reason word (because).
lessons.starter_activity: Recap signs of life from Monday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a sentence explaining why something is classified as alive, using 'because'.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 sentences explaining why chosen things are alive/dead/never alive.
key_questions: Can you use 'because' in your sentence?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note explanatory writing with reasoning — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.home_link: Explain why something is alive to your family.

lessons.title: Fraction Equivalence: 2/4 and 1/2
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recognise that 2/4 is equivalent to 1/2.
success_criteria: I can show 2/4 of a shape.
I can show it's the same as 1/2.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model showing 2/4 of a shape and comparing to 1/2, demonstrating equivalence.
lessons.independent_task: Children shade shapes to show 2/4 and 1/2, comparing and recording their equivalence.

differentiation.support: Adult supports comparison with folded shapes

lessons.assessment_notes: Record early fraction equivalence understanding, a new Year 2 concept — evidence for MATHS.N4.
lessons.home_link: Show 2/4 and 1/2 of something at home and compare.

lessons.title: Classifying Objects at Home and School
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to classify a wider range of objects as living, dead, or never alive.
success_criteria: I can classify an object correctly.
I can explain my reasoning using signs of life.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model classifying trickier examples (e.g. a fossil, a seed, a battery-powered toy).
lessons.independent_task: Children classify a range of objects found at home/school, recording reasoning.
resources_needed: Object picture cards including tricky examples
key_questions: Is this alive, dead, or never alive?
What sign of life helped you decide?

differentiation.greater_depth: Justify tricky examples using multiple signs of life

lessons.assessment_notes: Note deepening classification reasoning skill — evidence for SCI.LIV.
lessons.home_link: Classify 3 more objects at home with your family.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Living Things Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read living-things-themed words.
success_criteria: I can read living things words.
I can read a sentence about living things.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to living-things-themed words.
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading living things words over the week.

lessons.title: Tally Chart: Living Things Survey
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to record a survey about living things using a tally chart.
success_criteria: I can record a tally.
I can find the total.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model conducting a survey (e.g. types of pets owned) recording with tally marks.
lessons.independent_task: Children conduct and record a simple living-things-themed survey using tally marks.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record data handling consolidation — evidence for MATHS.STAT.
lessons.home_link: Do a simple tally survey with your family.

lessons.title: Are Fictional Characters Alive?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply classification knowledge to discuss fictional characters.
success_criteria: I can say if a fictional character would be 'alive' by science's definition.
I can explain my reasoning.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss a well-loved fictional character (e.g. a talking toy).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss the difference between fiction (things can be 'alive' in a story) and science's real classification.
lessons.independent_task: Children discuss and record whether a fictional character would count as alive scientifically, with reasoning.
resources_needed: Fictional character picture (from a story studied)
key_questions: Would this character be alive in real life?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain reasoning in detail using signs of life

lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of scientific reasoning to a creative context — evidence for SCI.LIV.
lessons.plenary: Recap the discussion about fiction vs reality.
lessons.home_link: Think of a fictional character and discuss with your family whether it would be 'alive'.

lessons.title: Living Things Debate: Is It Alive?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to discuss and justify a classification with evidence.
success_criteria: I can state my opinion.
I can give evidence for it.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap classification reasoning from the week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model stating a classification opinion with evidence for a tricky example.
lessons.independent_task: Children discuss a tricky classification example in small groups, justifying their view with evidence.

differentiation.greater_depth: Respond to a differing opinion respectfully with counter-evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note scientific reasoning and discussion skill — evidence for ENG.SL1/SCI.LIV.
lessons.plenary: Recap the range of views and evidence shared.
lessons.home_link: Discuss a tricky 'is it alive' example with your family.

lessons.title: Living Things Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction word problems using a living things context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap addition and subtraction strategies to 100.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems using a living things context (e.g. animals seen on a nature walk).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve living-things-themed word problems within 100, showing working.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill within 100 — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a living things word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Creating a Living Things Sorting Diagram
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create a sorting diagram to classify living things.
success_criteria: I can sort items into a diagram.
I can label my sorting categories.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all classification learning this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model creating a Venn or Carroll diagram to sort living/dead/never alive items.
lessons.independent_task: Children create their own sorting diagram, classifying a range of items.
key_questions: Which category does this belong in?
Can you label your diagram clearly?

differentiation.greater_depth: Create a diagram with 3+ overlapping categories

lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of classification to a structured diagram — evidence for SCI.LIV.
lessons.home_link: Sort objects at home into a simple diagram.

lessons.title: Living, Dead or Never Alive Quiz
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about living things classification.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about classifying living things, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: Why is a fossil not classed as living?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on living things facts you learned.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Fractions and Data
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply fraction and data handling skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can find a third of something.
I can read a tally chart.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of thirds, fraction equivalence, and tally charts.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: fractions, data handling.
key_questions: What is a third of this?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 4 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N4/STAT.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising thirds over the weekend.

lessons.title: Living Things Topic Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about classifying living things.
success_criteria: I can classify something as living, dead, or never alive.
I can explain my reasoning using signs of life.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering signs of life and classification.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet and contribute to a class 'Living, Dead or Never Alive' display.
key_questions: What have we learned about classifying living things?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: Note classification understanding progress, setting up habitats learning next week — evidence for SCI.LIV.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate the week's living things learning.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about living things with your family.
